notes.79v.17: cion is unidentified. ſ. (79v.19) is an unexplained abbreviation; ſe (79v.20) is taken as an abbreviated verb, '[sucks]'. Scotia may mean Ireland or Scotland.

nodes.text: or are held by any infirmity, drink it with honey and warm wine; it is effective.
[The herb] *cion* shines at night like a star, as the peony does. Whoever has it with him
ſ. never comes to harm. Take the skull from the head of a crow, and then,
when a child is born, before it [sucks] at its mother or any woman, squeeze from the breasts
[the milk] [of the mother] of the infant into the aforesaid crow's skull. Let the milk from the skull into the infant's mouth,
and so feed it for three days on end without other food. I heard an abbot from Upper
Scotia say with great assurance that afterwards, when the infant has grown,
it can distinguish all the calls of crows and their meanings.
